angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 557,256 km at 50.29 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 19.8858 +/- 0.0170 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 50.29 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.801 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Allart et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-69 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A...7A/abstract): 557,256 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.83 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Allart et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-69 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A...7A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4792 +/- 158 K from Allart et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-69 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A...7A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Allart et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-69 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A...7A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-69.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.550, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
